title: A map changes the question
hook: Present-day borders are not a fossil-age map.

knows: Fossils and models can supply evidence about the past.
doesNotKnow: The toy maps show two land areas joined in one state and separated in another. Past geography can change hypotheses about possible connections; a map alone does not prove a route taken by a particular animal.

misconception: Present-day geography alone is sufficient for every deep-time fossil comparison.
objective: When comparing two fossil localities, why might researchers consider continental positions at the time rather than only today’s map?

recall.question: Two land areas are separated today but joined in an illustrated past map. What does that change?
options: A specific animal route is proven
All fossil dates become the same
A past land connection becomes a hypothesis to investigate
